syntheses.title: Comparison of Modular Pipeline and Imitation Learning Performance in Autonomous Driving
syntheses.body: Paper A reports that the performance difference between the modular pipeline and imitation learning methods is less than 10% (claim 32a49fa0-8395-506b-9794-efc1f7fa2a8f). Additionally, Paper A notes that the modular pipeline's performance is bimodal depending on perception stack success (claim 878110a6-7623-50b9-ab7c-962de08a0fea). Paper B finds that pure imitation learning is insufficient even with large datasets and mid-level input/output representations (claim 639f88c8-001d-587a-bae9-390fb3c89dcf), and that imitation dropout improves driving model performance compared to under-weighting imitation losses (claims fab08fe9-9a3f-574a-80b1-ef95478330f6 and f1f0ef71-20f9-593d-a66f-3cf2bb27c155). Thus, the two papers provide complementary insights comparing modular pipeline and imitation learning methods in autonomous driving contexts.
